publication.title: iPhone OS Research Atlas
publication.scope: iPhone OS 1.1.4 / 4A102 and 3.1.3 / 7E18; native PinePhone execution, distinct QEMU gates and offline next-target study
publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.

record.title: Physical MMC mapping advances a timeout frontier
record.method: Retained matched controller-mapping controls and UART checkpoints
record.observation: In the early physical 4A102 MMC2 trial, non-cacheable controller mapping advances the clock-update timeout to a separate NTSR admission fault. Correcting the unsupported NTSR readback requirement reaches block-device/root discovery.
record.limits: This September 26 control does not establish an HFS mount, launchd, graphical use, persistent physical writes or a known reset cause. Later storage acceptance has separate records.
record.status: Historical bounded physical control; incomplete boot retained

excerpts.content:
{
  "/controls/0/observation": "Original XNU verbose UART, MMC2 clock-update timeout at stage 5, BSD root wait for disk0s1",
  "/controls/1/observation": "MMC2 CMD remained 0x80202000 and NTSR read 0x80000000 through the original late I/O mapping",
  "/controls/2/observation": "Non-cacheable mapping changed NTSR readback to 0; the old mandatory readback check stopped at stage 3",
  "/source_correction": "A64 MMC2 NTSR bit 31 must not be required to read back after a write",
  "/successful_mmc2_run/hfs_root_mount_observed": false,
  "/successful_mmc2_run/launchd_observed": false
}
